problems.title: A middle geometric-progression term
problems.question: $b_8=10,b_{12}=8/5$. Find $b_{10}$.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate formula, simplify it, and check the conditions.
steps: Then $b_{10}=10(2/5)=4$. It is positive even if $q$ is negative.

problems.title: Sum only the positive terms
problems.question: Find the sum of positive terms of $a_n=20-2n/3$, starting with $n=1$.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate formula, simplify it, and check the conditions.
steps: There are 29 positive terms. The first is $58/3$ and last $2/3$.

problems.title: Points equidistant from three lines
problems.question: How many points have equal distances from $2x+4y=7$, $4x+8y=11$, $3x+2y=1$?
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate formula, simplify it, and check the conditions.
formulas: The equidistant locus of two distinct parallel lines is their midline.
steps: Normalize the second line to $2x+4y=11/2$. The first two lines have a unique parallel midline, and their distance from every point on it is a fixed positive number $d$.
Points at distance $d$ from the third line lie on its two parallel offsets. Each meets the midline once because the third line is not parallel to the first two.

problems.question: $A=(1,1),B=(2,5),C=(6,3)$ and $M$ is the centroid. Find vector $MA$.

problems.title: Starting one doubling ahead
problems.question: A population’s infected count starts at 1 and doubles daily, reaching everyone on day 200. If it starts at 2, on which day does it reach everyone?
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate formula, simplify it, and check the conditions.
formulas: Day-$n$ count from a start of 1 is $2^{n-1}$.
steps: With a start of 2, the day-$n$ count is $2^n$, exactly the old day-$(n+1)$ count.
Therefore the threshold is reached one day earlier, on day 199.

problems.title: Recover a term from partial sums
problems.question: $S_n=n^2+2n$. Find the 99th term.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate formula, simplify it, and check the conditions.
steps: At $n=99$, this is 199.

problems.title: Median of five geometric terms
problems.question: $b_1>0$ and the median of $b_1,\ldots,b_5$ equals $b_1$. Which listed ratio works?
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate formula, simplify it, and check the conditions.
formulas: A median is the third value after sorting; scale all terms by positive $b_1$.
steps: The listed ratio $q=-2$ gives normalized values $1,-2,4,-8,16$. Sorting yields $-8,-2,1,4,16$, whose median is 1.
The other listed positive ratios have median $q^2\ne1$. For the listed negative fractions, two positive later terms are below 1, so the median is below 1.

problems.title: Perpendicular vector combinations
problems.question: Nonzero vectors $a,b$ have equal lengths; $a+2b$ is perpendicular to $3a-b$. Find the cosine of their angle.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate formula, simplify it, and check the conditions.
steps: Expand: $(a+2b)\cdot(3a-b)=3|a|^2+5a\cdot b-2|b|^2=0$.
Let their common length be $r>0$. Then $r^2+5r^2\cos\theta=0$, giving $\cos\theta=-1/5$.

problems.title: Complete squares in a circle equation
problems.question: Find the radius of $x^2+y^2+2x-4y+1=0$.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate formula, simplify it, and check the conditions.
steps: Complete the squares: $(x+1)^2+(y-2)^2=4$.
The centre is $(-1,2)$ and the radius is 2.

problems.title: A die with repeated labels
problems.question: A fair six-faced die has one face labelled 1, two labelled 2 and three labelled 3. Find the probability that two independent rolls sum to 4.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate formula, simplify it, and check the conditions.
steps: The disjoint possibilities are $(1,3),(3,1),(2,2)$.

problems.title: A random point on a segment
problems.question: $M$ is chosen uniformly on a segment of length 12. Find the probability that neither resulting piece exceeds 8.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate formula, simplify it, and check the conditions.
steps: Let $AM=x$, so $BM=12-x$. Both are at most 8 exactly when $4\le x\le8$.
The favourable interval has length 4, so the probability is $4/12=1/3$.

problems.title: At least one passes: an unstated assumption
problems.question: Two students pass with probabilities 0.2 and 0.3. Find the probability that at least one passes.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate formula, simplify it, and check the conditions.
steps: The given information gives $P(A\cup B)=0.5-P(A\cap B)$, but does not specify the intersection.
The intersection can range from 0 to 0.2, so the union can be any value from 0.3 to 0.5.
If independence is additionally assumed, the intersection is $0.2(0.3)=0.06$ and the answer becomes $0.44$.
problems.answer: Not uniquely determined; 0.44 under an independence assumption.
problems.note: The source does not explicitly state independence. The listed intended choice 0.44 requires that extra condition.

problems.title: An internal-division vector
problems.question: $BM:CM=1:3$ and $AM=\alpha AB+\beta AC$. Find $\alpha-\beta$ (all symbols here denote vectors).
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate formula, simplify it, and check the conditions.
steps: Subtract $A$: $AM=(3/4)AB+(1/4)AC$.
Thus $\alpha-\beta=3/4-1/4=1/2$.

problems.title: Dot products of regular-hexagon sides
problems.question: For regular hexagon $ABCDEF$, find $(AB\cdot BC)/(BC\cdot DE)$, using directed side vectors.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate formula, simplify it, and check the conditions.
steps: Successive side directions turn by $60^\circ$. Thus the numerator is $s^2\cos60^\circ=s^2/2$.
The directions of $BC$ and $DE$ differ by $120^\circ$, so the denominator is $-s^2/2$. The ratio is $-1$.

problems.title: Sum an infinite geometric series
problems.question: $b_1=\alpha,b_2=\beta$ and $|q|<1$. Find the infinite sum.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate formula, simplify it, and check the conditions.
steps: Substitute the ratio: $S=\alpha/(1-\beta/\alpha)=\alpha^2/(\alpha-\beta)$.
problems.note: The usual geometric-progression convention assumes a nonzero first term so the ratio is defined. The identically zero sequence separately has sum zero.

problems.title: Median and a unique mode
problems.question: The data $x,y,2,7,11,9$ have median 6 and unique mode 2. Find their mean.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate formula, simplify it, and check the conditions.
formulas: For six sorted values, median is the average of the third and fourth.
steps: At least one of $x,y$ must be 2. If both are 2, the median is $(2+7)/2=4.5$, so exactly one is 2.
The other value must be 5: sorted data become $2,2,5,7,9,11$, giving median 6 and unique mode 2. Values outside the interval $(2,7)$ cannot give median 6.
The sum is 36 and the mean is $36/6=6$.

problems.title: The last consecutive even number
problems.question: There are $n$ consecutive even natural numbers, the smallest $m$. Find the largest.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate formula, simplify it, and check the conditions.
steps: Start at $m$ and make $n-1$ steps of size 2. The largest is $m+2(n-1)$.

problems.title: Collinear coordinate vectors
problems.question: Find $k$ if $(k-2,k+2)$ is collinear with $(6,14)$.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate formula, simplify it, and check the conditions.
formulas: Two planar vectors are collinear iff their determinant is zero.
steps: Thus $k=5$.

problems.title: Intersection of triangle altitudes
problems.question: $A=(1,1),B=(2,5),C=(4,3)$. Find the orthocenter.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate formula, simplify it, and check the conditions.
formulas: Perpendicular nonvertical lines have slopes whose product is $-1$.
steps: $BC$ has slope $-1$, so the altitude from $A$ is $y=x$. $AB$ has slope 4, so the altitude from $C$ is $y-3=-(x-4)/4$.
Substitute $y=x$: $4x-12=-x+4$, hence $x=y=16/5$.

problems.title: The range of combined data
problems.question: Two data sets have ranges 19 and 24. Which listed value can be the range of their union?
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate formula, simplify it, and check the conditions.
formulas: The union range is at least the larger individual range.
steps: The combined range must be at least 24. Among the listed numbers $199,22,19,5,1$, only 199 qualifies.
It is achievable: use the sets $\{0,19\}$ and $\{175,199\}$. Their individual ranges are 19 and 24 and their union range is 199.

problems.title: Mutually exclusive is not the same as independent
problems.question: How many of the six printed probability identities always hold for disjoint events $A,B$?
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate formula, simplify it, and check the conditions.
steps: The first and sixth identities are exactly these two rules.
The sum need not be 1: choose probabilities $1/4,1/4$. Their product need not be zero either, so neither the product-zero identities nor independence identity is automatic.

problems.title: Sum of divisors of a prime power
problems.question: Find the sum of all positive divisors of $199^{199}$.
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate formula, simplify it, and check the conditions.
formulas: For prime $p$, divisors of $p^n$ are $1,p,\ldots,p^n$; their sum is $(p^{n+1}-1)/(p-1)$.
steps: 199 is prime: none of $2,3,5,7,11,13$, the primes at most $\sqrt{199}$, divides it.
Apply the geometric-series formula with $p=199,n=199$.

problems.title: A line tangent to a circle
problems.question: Which listed line is tangent to $x^2+y^2=2$?
problems.idea: Set up the appropriate formula, simplify it, and check the conditions.
steps: The radius is $\sqrt2$. For $x+y=2$, the centre-to-line distance is $2/\sqrt2=\sqrt2$, so it is tangent.
The other listed lines have distances $2,2\sqrt2,4,1,2$, all different from the radius.
